sources.title: Kevin S. Tracy, A Square-Root Kalman Filter Using Only QR Decompositions
sources.locator: Complete four-page paper inspected; §§2–3.4, equations (3)–(7), (17)–(36), and Algorithm 1.

contents.name: §2, equations (3)–(7), QR factor of a sum of covariance factors
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the exact Gram identity with rectangular factors, zero padding, and rank loss.

contents.name: §§3.1–3.2, QR prediction, innovation factor, and triangular gain solve
contents.reason: The local algorithm specifies a finite horizon, arbitrary rectangular input factors, its unpivoted Householder QR loop, and explicit status branches.

contents.name: §3.3, Joseph-form and square-root covariance update
contents.reason: The local block-Gram proof derives its own measurement array and exactly identifies the canonical Schur complement.

contents.name: §3.4, Algorithm 1, prediction/innovation/update sequence
contents.reason: The local procedure fixes operation order, padding, sign normalization, range outcomes, and finite-horizon accuracy reporting.

contents.name: §§3.2–3.4, triangular innovation solve and covariance update
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the gain and solve-residual bounds with explicit innovation and data-scale factors.

contents.name: §3.4, finite Algorithm 1 loop and bounded filter cycle
contents.reason: The local theorem proves finite status behavior for the specified padded and budgeted implementation.

sources.title: M. A. Salzmann, Some Aspects of Kalman Filtering, Technical Report 140
sources.locator: Full-text PDF retrieved; Chapter 3, §3.3.1 (printed pp. 30–31) and §3.5.2 (printed p. 42) inspected.

contents.name: §3.3.1, square-root covariance time and measurement updates
contents.reason: The local proof derives the block QR equations and allows singular posterior factors and positive innovation only.

contents.name: §3.3.1, covariance square root as a factor product
contents.reason: The local algebra gives the exact factor-product positivity and quantitative perturbation bound.

contents.name: §3.5.2, stability applies to covariance updates, not automatically to gain or estimate
contents.reason: The local theorem supplies separate conditioned gain, solve, mean, covariance, and finite-horizon bounds rather than assuming gain/estimate stability.

contents.name: §3.5.1, finite-operation accounting for one filter cycle
contents.reason: The local proof shows termination from the finite horizon, finite dimensions, and finite component procedures.

sources.title: Simo Särkkä, Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing, Cambridge University Press
sources.locator: Full-text PDF retrieved; Chapter 4 §§4.1–4.3, especially Theorem 4.2 and equations (4.20)–(4.29), printed pp. 51–58, inspected.

contents.name: §4.3, Theorem 4.2 and equations (4.20)–(4.21), exact Kalman prediction and update
contents.reason: The local block proof independently recovers these canonical mean and covariance maps without restating the Gaussian derivation.

contents.name: §4.3, equations (4.27)–(4.29), joint Gaussian conditioning and Schur complement
contents.reason: The algorithm implements this canonical recursion by triangular factors and exact QR identities.

contents.name: §4.3, square-root methods as a numerical-stability motivation
contents.reason: The example gives an exact binary floating-point witness for the cancellation risk; it does not use the source as a proof.

contents.name: §4.3, finite-horizon Kalman recursion
contents.reason: The local result makes termination and status behavior explicit for the finite recursion.
